In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: SVM: Trigger new ASID allocation in both VMCBs on pCPU switch

When the pCPU where the VMCB was most recently used is switched, reset
the ASID generation in both VMCBs, triggering new ASID allocation for
the immediate VMRUN as well as the next VMRUN on the other VMCB.

The ASID is shared between vmcb01 and vmcb02, and gets flushed on every
nested transition. However, since pCPU tracking is done per VMCB, it is
possible for one VMCB to allocate a new ASID when migrated to a new
pCPU, and then the other VMCB reuses that ASID on the old pCPU. This can
result in the same ASID being used by multiple vCPUs on the old pCPU.

Example scenario:
- vCPU runs on pCPU A, vmcb01 is active, asid=1.
- vCPU migrates to pCPU B, vmcb01 pCPU changes, new asid=2.
- Another vCPU runs on pCPU A and allocates asid=2 as well.
- vCPU migrates back to pCPU A, and then switches to vmcb02 before it
runs again with vmcb01.
- No pCPU switch…

CVE-2026-99669.title: mm/huge_memory: fix truncate racing with PMD zapping
CVE-2026-99669.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: fix truncate racing with PMD zapping

zap_huge_pmd_folio() removes the rmap before calling folio_mark_dirty().
If this was the last mapping, truncation can skip unmapping the folio
and proceed without waiting for the PMD lock, racing with dirtying.

ifs_set_range_dirty() can oops if MADV_DONTNEED races with
ftruncate() on XFS, when we get the folio set dirty after it was found
to not be mapped anymore.

Move folio_mark_dirty() and folio_mark_accessed() before rmap removal,
matching the PTE zap path. This keeps the folio mapped while updating
its state, so truncation must wait for the page table lock.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

CVE-2026-9239.title: Meow Gallery <= 5.5.1 - Authenticated (Author+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Attachment Alt Text (aria-label attribute)
CVE-2026-9239.description: The Meow Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Attachment Alt Text (aria-label attribute) in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The vulnerable code path is only reachable when a gallery item is rendered as a link (i.e., link_href is non-empty), and exploitation relies on the fact that WordPress's sanitize_text_field() strips angle-bracketed tags but preserves double quotes, allowing an attacker to break out of the aria-label attribute context and inject event-handler attributes such as onclick.
